en: So I'm back in my course project and I'm in
an existing session. I resumed that session
from earlier where we added a new feature,
where we added that posting feature.
Now in that session, I already consumed
around 30% of my context window, but that
means there still is plenty of space in that
context window. So I might want to continue
with the next features in that session here,
but I might wanna continue in 2 different
ways.
Let's say first I wanna perform a code
review.
I know I already did that in a different
session before, but let's say I wanna code
review just these changes here.
And second, I want to continue working
on the next feature and I wanna do that side
by side.
Now of course I can start a new session
in a separate terminal window, for example.
So now I got 2 PySessions and in that second
terminal window I could
add my code review prompt and tell it to
review the code that was last edited. So not
the entire codebase, but just this feature
that was recently added
in that last commit, which it finds. And
that would work.
But of course, we already have a session
with all the knowledge we need for reviewing
just that code and not the entire codebase.
So it's kind of unnecessary to point it at a
specific commit and hope that it finds the
right context when it's already here? That's
where we could use the /clone command
because clone duplicates the current
session.
So if we take a look at these files, you see
right now there are 3, 4, 5 session files
here. If I run
/clone now,
this was cloned to a new session
and now we have 6 session files instead of
This one here is brand new,
but this one is exactly the same as the old
session file. But if we now continue, the
context we're adding here will only be in
the new session file, not in the old one. So
we have the old session twice and we can
continue down 2 different paths.
Therefore, if I now open a new PySession
with -r to resume a session,
I can resume that old session and it's also
visually represented here. We got the
original session here and then the clone
here, and these are now 2 separate sessions.
So here I'll continue the original one,
and in my
other window where I ran clone, I'll also
run
/resume,
and then I'll continue this cloned one. And
I actually am already in there, as I can see
since it's light blue, but if I wanted to be
sure, I could select it. So now I'm in 2
different sessions even though they have the
same stem, they have the same context in
there. All the context up to this point
where I ran clone is available in both
sessions. But if we now continue, we
continue with fresh context that's then
exclusive per session. That's the idea
behind clone.
And so now in one session I could perform my
code review,
in the other session I could start working
on the next feature.
Now before we do that, however,
Let me show you
/fork because that's very similar to /clone.
